narrative.overview:
A fan's paper scorebook, kept under the Green Monster. Every surface is either the Monster-green wall (the frame around everything), the dark board pages laid on it (sheets), or the cream ink a scorekeeper writes with. The game is told in scorebook notation: diamonds per plate appearance, play codes like 6-3 and F8, and fielder sequences. The rest of the app, from leaderboards to profiles and game logs, is kept with the same pencil.

The mood is precise, spare and scorekeeper-like. The old-ballpark character lives in the type, the notation and a few physical scoreboard parts, not in ornament. Numbers carry the page; captions, legends and helper text are left out because these readers know baseball. Color is rationed: cream for everything that is simply true, gold for the scoreboard's trim and for what is excellent, and brick red only for outs and runs against.

Components split by role. Data and identity get physical scoreboard parts: recessed number slots, pegged nameplates and award plates. Controls and navigation stay quiet: thin rules, soft labels and square segments that recede until touched.
keyCharacteristics: Monster-green frame, dark board sheets, cream ink. Three layers, always in that order.
Square corners everywhere except the 2px recessed slot and round data dots.
Condensed Oswald for names and numbers; small-caps Overpass for every label.
Gold does two jobs: trim in the scheme (section titles, active and focus rules), and earned in the data (elite rank, quality start, award).
Zeros left blank in tables, so the cells that carry ink are the ones that happened.

rules.name: The Monster Stays Rule
rules.body: The frame is Monster Green and never darkens or shifts. Text on the frame is full Scorekeeper Cream. Small or secondary text belongs on a board plate, not directly on the wall.

rules.name: The Two Golds Rule
rules.body: Gold has two jobs, and they don't mix. As trim it is simply part of the scheme, like the paint on a scoreboard: section titles, the active tab and segment rules, focus rings, the jersey number, the wash on the user's own team. In the data it is earned: a number, dot, lamp or mark turns gold only for excellence or a positive event (top 10% of that season's qualified pool, a quality start, an award, a hit, an RBI, a made 5-star catch). Trim never reaches into the data: a value is never gold just to lead the eye, so a "lead stat" stays cream.

rules.name: The Blank Zero Rule
rules.body: In game logs and tables, a zero count is left blank, never written as 0. The exceptions are pairs read aloud ("0-4" H-AB, an inning pitched), a linescore or big-number summary, where a blank would read as missing, and a zero that is the achievement (a starter's 0 ER or 0 BB on the Highlights tab).

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every column of numbers uses tabular figures, so ranks, averages and scores line up digit for digit.

rules.name: The Painted Label Rule
rules.body: Labels sit above what they name, in small uppercase Overpass with wide tracking, like paint on a scoreboard. A value is never prefixed inline with its abbreviation ("Ht / Wt …") when a labelled pair fits.

rules.name: The Fixed Slot Rule
rules.body: Any control whose content changes, such as a filter select, a stat column or a swipe card, gets a fixed slot sized for its longest real value. Changing a filter must never shift the row around it.

rules.name: The Pressed, Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Numbers sit in slots pressed into the board; names hang on plates in front of it. Data is never raised on a card.

rules.name: The Shared Edge Rule
rules.body: Two sections side by side are a pair, and a pair shares its top and bottom edge. Pair sections whose natural heights are close; then the shorter one fills by spreading its own tiles or cells, and a board whose rows mean something (standings) keeps its condensed height and sets the pair's, its partner sized to end on its last row. Never leave one column running short beside another.

dos: **Do** keep the Monster Green frame (#54796d) exactly. Fix contrast by changing what sits on it.
**Do** put numbers in recessed slots and clickable names on pegged nameplates.
**Do** leave zero counts blank in logs and tables.
**Do** use Pennant Gold as trim (section titles, active and focus rules) and, within the data, only for top-10% stats, made 5-star catches, quality starts, awards, RBIs and hits.
**Do** use tabular figures for every column of numbers.
**Do** size changeable controls to fixed slots so filters never shift the layout.
**Do** draw spray charts in the API's own coordinate space (home 125.42, 198.27; 2.495 ft per unit) so fences and batted balls agree.
**Do** give sections that sit side by side a shared top and bottom edge (the Shared Edge Rule).
donts: **Don't** round corners on plates, cards, buttons or selects. Only slots (2px), bar ends (3px) and dots are rounded.
**Don't** use Faded Cream for text on the green frame. It fails contrast there.
**Don't** add helper captions, legends or tutorial text. These users know baseball.
**Don't** make a value gold that hasn't earned it, such as a "lead stat"; trim stays out of the data.
**Don't** use nameplates for identity that isn't a link, such as a profile's own team and position.
**Don't** let a zero-based scale waste half a bar. Start the axis near the data and label both ends.
